plan.title: Muscle treated vs control DE with outlier sensitivity
plan.analytical_narrative: Ten samples (5 treated, 5 control) of human muscle bulk RNA-seq raw Salmon gene counts (12000 genes x 10 samples in the count matrix, plus 1 gene-symbol column) are analyzed for differential expression between treated and control. The data profile flags sample_03 as separating from its group on PCA and the sample distance heatmap. Per the grounded procedure, this outlier is investigated but not silently removed: QC first characterizes it (library size, detected-gene count, clustering) so a technical cause can be stated if one exists; the DESeq2 Wald model is then fit twice — once on all 10 samples and once with sample_03 excluded — and both gene lists are reported side by side with their overlap, so the primary conclusion is not silently contingent on one sample. Raw counts are modeled directly in DESeq2 (median-of-ratios normalization internal to the model, no pre-normalization), low-count genes are minimally pre-filtered, the Wald test's log2 fold changes are shrunk with apeglm for reporting/ranking, and BH-adjusted p-values with independent filtering select the differentially expressed set at alpha=0.05. The Wald statistic ranks all tested genes for a preranked fgsea analysis against MSigDB Hallmark (primary) and Reactome (follow-up), both staged locally for human. A final report step consolidates diagnostics (PCA, sample-distance heatmap, MA plot, dispersion plot, p-value histogram), the two DE gene lists with their intersection, the enrichment results with leading-edge genes, and a full reproducibility record.

input.query: org.Hs.eg.db entrez mapping human gene identifier

Keep genes with >=10 counts in >=5 samples (smallest group size)
DESeq2 design ~condition with explicit reference level = control
DESeq2 Wald test, run twice (all 10 samples; and n=9 with outlier removed)
fgsea preranked GSEA on Wald statistic, MSigDB Hallmark then Reactome
Combined DE + enrichment report with sensitivity comparison
